sources.title: Mount Qingcheng - Chengdu Travel Guide
sources.content:
Mount Qingcheng is considered the home of Taoism (Daoism) and is one of the most important Taoist sites in China. The name means green city, reflecting peaks densely forested with trees, bamboo, caves, and scenic locations.

Two Mountains: The area comprises Qingcheng (Front) Mountain and Qingcheng Back Mountain, situated approximately 80 kilometers west of Chengdu. The Front Mountain features Taoist temples and shorter hikes, attracting most visitors. Back Mountain offers natural scenery ideal for experienced hikers.

What to Expect: Visitors should anticipate significant walking and climbing. The steps are uneven and narrow in spots, and they can get slippery when wet. Despite challenges, the experience delivers beautiful scenery surrounded by vegetation and panoramic views from higher elevations.

Practical Tips: Use cable cars if time is limited. Hire a guide for navigation. Wear comfortable clothing and sturdy shoes. Arrive early to avoid crowds. Bring snacks and water (refreshments available but expensive). Summer visits are challenging due to heat and humidity.

Hours & Fees:
- Hours: 8:00 AM-6:00 PM (March-November); 8:30 AM-5:00 PM (December-March)
- Entrance: 80 RMB (Front); 20 RMB (Back)
- Cable cars: 30-80 RMB
- Duration: Half-day to full day

Transportation: Take Subway Line 2 to Xibu station, then high-speed train (30 minutes, 10 RMB) to Dujiangyan Station. Shuttle buses connect to mountains. Alternatively, taxi/car takes approximately 1.5 hours from downtown Chengdu.

sources.title: Qingchengshan Travel Guide, Mount Qingcheng Tours
sources.content:
Qingchengshan is situated 54km southwest of Chengdu city in Sichuan Province and represents one of China's ancient Taoist centers. The mountain features luxuriant and verdant trees and is praised as the most peaceful and secluded mountain under heaven.

Recommended Visit Length: 0.5 to 1 day.

Main Attractions:
Taoist Heritage: The mountain contains significant Taoism temples. Jianfu Temple at the base dates to the Tang Dynasty. Tianshi Cave, midway up, was the teaching location of Zhang Daolin, an influential Taoist master. Sangqing Temple at the peak originated during the Jin Dynasty with current Qing Dynasty structures.

Natural Features: The landscape features countless peaks and densely covered by ancient trees. The posterior (back) mountain offers more secluded scenery with over 80km of hiking trails.

Hiking: The site offers excellent trekking opportunities combining physical activity with traditional Taoist shrine experiences.

Visitor Information:
Operating Hours: 08:00-16:30
Entrance Fees: Base admission 80 RMB, Cable car 60 RMB, Ferry 10 RMB, Golf car 35 RMB.

Qingcheng Back Mountain: Less-visited Buddhist location with lower entrance costs (20 RMB) and lighter crowds.

Best Time to Visit: Summer offers cooler temperatures (approximately 15°C annually). The region experiences frequent rain and fog.

Transportation: Express service from Chengdu North Station (50 minutes, 15 RMB), followed by bus No. 101. Shuttle service from Chadianzi Tourism Bus Station (approximately 1 hour).

Qingcheng Four Wonders food specialties: White Fruit Stewed Chicken, Qingcheng Pickles, Dongtian Rice Wine, and Qingcheng Tea.

sources.title: Mount Qingcheng National Park Guide (China, 2026)
sources.content:
Mount Qingcheng is a famous Taoist sacred mountain and UNESCO World Heritage Site located about 68 kilometers southwest of Chengdu, with a history over 2,000 years as the cradle of Taoism.

Getting There: The fastest way is taking Chengdu Metro Line 2 to Xibu Station, then transferring to a Chengdu-Guanxian intercity train bound for Qingchengshan Station, with trains running every 20-30 minutes and total travel time of about 1.5 hours.

Tickets & Hours: Opens 8:00-17:30 (April-October) / 8:30-17:00 (November-March), with tickets costing ¥80.

Key Tips: Wear comfortable sports shoes as paths are steep in some areas, and bring a light jacket since mountain temperature is 5-8°C lower than Chengdu. Using Didi ride-sharing is the best way to get there, taking about 45 minutes and being cheap and easier than public transport.

Mount Qingcheng is divided into Front Mountain (cultural sites) and Back Mountain (natural hiking), with the Front Mountain being the highlight for most visitors.

sources.title: 青城山 - 百度百科
sources.content:
青城山位于四川省成都市都江堰市西南，距成都68千米。作为世界文化遗产，国家5A级旅游景区，这座山以其独特的自然和文化价值而闻名。

地理特征：该景区占地面积200平方千米，最高峰老君阁海拔1260米。山区属于亚热带季风性湿润气候，林木青翠，四季常青，诸峰环峙，状若城廓，因此得名青城山。

历史文化：东汉汉安二年，张道陵到达青城山，结茅传道，创立了道教。这使得青城山成为中国四大道教名山之首。山上存有多处道教宫观，包括天师洞、上清宫、建福宫等。

主要景点：前山景区包括老君阁、天师洞、上清宫等文物古迹。后山区域面积约100平方千米，以水秀、林幽、山雄著称，其中有金壁天仓、圣母洞等景观。

旅游信息：景区全年开放，旺季（3月2日至11月30日）开放时间为08:00-17:00，门票价格为成人90元。可乘坐动车直达青城山站。

青城山享有青城天下幽的美誉，是中国四大道教名山之一、五大仙山之一、成都十景之一。全山林木青翠，群峰环绕起伏、林木葱茏幽翠。

东汉顺帝初年，张道陵入鹤鸣山修道，创立五斗米道（天师道），最早从鹤鸣山来到青城山结茅传道，并羽化山中。

sources.title: Mount Qingcheng - Chengdu, Mt. Qingcheng - China Discovery
sources.content:
Mount Qingcheng is a famous Taoism mountain in China. The page covers Mount Qingcheng as a UNESCO World Heritage Site with sections addressing attractions, temples, activities, travel routes, optimal visiting seasons, lodging options, and visitor guidance.

The mountain is divided into Front Mountain (cultural sites with Taoist temples) and Back Mountain (natural scenery with hiking trails). Most tourists visit the Front Mountain for its Taoist heritage and temples.

Key temples include Jianfu Temple at the base, Tianshi Cave midway (the teaching location of Zhang Daolin), and Shangqing Palace at the peak.

The mountain can be combined with a visit to nearby Dujiangyan Irrigation System for a full day trip from Chengdu.
